_doc: REGISTRATION ONLY. Makes bench's own verify/ entrypoints available as
named checks a run may ask for. It declares NO gates block, so every
gate reads `ungated`: nothing is required and nothing is proved by
registering a check. Inactive until a person copies it to
manager/local/profiles.json (or points BOARD_AGENT_PROFILES at it).
One name per check, asked for by work, act-pr and review alike. Each
runs at root `source`: a detached checkout bench makes of the card's
branch tip, so the program that runs is the one committed in the
candidate (never the operator's installation or the application's main
checkout), the source is clean by construction, and the evidence is
bound to the commit a gate reads. A review's `source` is the card's
branch tip in this checkout, not the pull request head bench pins for
the review: when the two differ the evidence names the branch commit,
and a gate compares that against the head it is about to merge. It is
NOT evidence about the pull request's proposed head.
For that, review alone also offers bench-backend-proposed and
bench-docs-proposed at root `review`: the detached checkout bench pinned
to the head the pull request proposes. They are optional and differently
named on purpose, so no gate that requires bench-backend can be satisfied
by them, and no same-head assurance is claimed for the `source` names.
bench-backend refuses ANY skipped test (setup-error): the suite skips
rather than fails without node or markdown-it-py, and `OK (skipped=121)`
is not a pass of the whole suite. Its required preparation,
`verify/preflight backend`, makes that prepare-failed by name instead.
Each check names a REQUIRED preparation step, verify/preflight. Bench
records a non-zero check exit as `failed`, whatever the check meant by
it — it has no other word. A required step that exits non-zero is
`prepare-failed`, with the check never run, which is the honest word
for a missing dependency or a browser that cannot start its sandbox.
Other setup errors inside a check (a test module that cannot import, a
disposable backend that will not start) still exit 2 and still read
`failed` in bench's evidence; the check's own record and log say
setup-error.
bench-docs and its preflight use `python3`. The docs builder needs
markdown-it-py: point both at a virtualenv you own (append
`--python /abs/venv/bin/python` to both runs) or it is prepare-failed.
work and act-pr keep the legacy grant BOARD_AGENT_COMMANDS gave them
(`python3 -m unittest`) as a named command grant: writing a document
replaces the legacy resolution for an intent it configures, so a
document that dropped it would quietly take the agent's own test runs
away.
